title: Check yourself: the trade-offs between checked and unchecked

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, how does choosing a checked or an unchecked exception affect performance?

options.text: Unchecked ones cost less, since no handler has to be generated
options.says: The page says the choice makes no difference at run time.

options.text: Checked ones cost less, since their handlers are bound at compile time
options.says: The page says the choice makes no difference at run time; both kinds fill in a stack trace when created.

options.text: Neither costs less: both fill in a stack trace when they are created
options.says: The page's answer on performance: no run-time difference, and the stack trace is the cost either way.

questions.stem: Per this page, which drawback comes with preferring unchecked exceptions?

options.text: Methods that throw them fit badly with lambdas and streams
options.says: The page lists fitting better with lambdas as an advantage of unchecked exceptions.

options.text: The compiler no longer makes callers consider the failure
options.says: The page names reduced compile-time safety: developers may overlook exceptions they are not forced to handle.

options.text: A new failure mode added to an API breaks existing callers
options.says: The page says unchecked exceptions let an API add failure modes without breaking compatibility.

concepts: Checked or unchecked makes no difference at run time; both fill in a stack trace when created.
Preferring unchecked exceptions costs compile-time safety, so documentation matters more.
